hits: The check `input.party >= table.seats` refuses a party that exactly fills the table. A 4-seat table rejects a change to 4 with PartyTooLarge, and the message then reads 'seats 4, not 4'. `create_booking` uses `>` and accepts such a party, so the two commands disagree. The tests only try 3 and 5, so they don't catch it.

delete executes the SQL delete but never commits, unlike save and add_tables. The change is only visible on this connection and is lost if the process exits before another commit; the cancel route still returns 204. The shared repository test uses the same connection, so it does not catch this.

The duplicate check also requires `b.table_id == input.table_id`, so a guest who already has a booking that day can still book a different table. The failure message and the test name both say one booking per guest per day. The test only covers the same-table case, so it misses this.

The check `OPENING < input.slot.start` uses a strict comparison, so a booking at exactly 17:00 is refused. The error message itself says bookings are taken from 17:00. The tests cover 16:30 and 21:30 but not 17:00, so this boundary is untested.

The conflict loop calls booking_at(table.id, input.slot) instead of the loop variable slot, so it checks the first week on every iteration. A conflict in week 2 or later is never detected, so the command books over an existing reservation instead of returning SlotTaken, which breaks the all-or-nothing promise.

The party-size check loads `booking.table_id`, which is the booking's current table, and the party already fits there. The booking is moving to `other.table_id`, so that is the table whose seats should be checked. As written, a party of 4 on t1 can be swapped onto the 2-seat t2 and `PartyTooLarge` is never returned. The tests don't cover this case.

`booked_tables` is built from `b.id` (booking ids), but is compared against table ids (`t.id`) on the next line. No table id matches a booking id, so `empty_tables` always equals the total number of tables, even on days with bookings. The test also never asserts `empty_tables`, so the bug is not caught.
